draft.title: Musculoskeletal injuries
card: Musculoskeletal injuries affect bones, joints, muscles, tendons and ligaments. They are grouped by how fast they develop.
an injury that happens suddenly, often from one event such as a fall, a tackle or a bad landing. A sprain is a stretched or torn ligament. A strain is a stretched or torn muscle or tendon.
a problem that develops slowly over weeks, months or years. Examples are overtraining syndrome, arthritis and osteoporosis.

Overtraining syndrome comes from too much training without enough rest. Arthritis is joint pain and stiffness from inflamed joints. Osteoporosis is a loss of bone density that makes bones weaker and easier to break.
draft.remember: Acute injuries come on suddenly. Chronic problems build up over time.

a.q: Which of these is an acute musculoskeletal injury?
opts: A sprained ankle from landing badly after a jump
Osteoporosis that has slowly weakened the bones
Arthritis that has stiffened the knee over years
Overtraining syndrome after months of heavy training
a.why: A sprain happens suddenly, from one event such as a bad landing. The other three develop gradually over a long time, so they are chronic.
a.clue: Look for the one that happens in a single moment.

b.q: Priya is a distance runner. Over several months she trains six days a week with no rest. She becomes tired, her times get worse and her mood drops. What is the best description of her problem?
opts: A chronic problem, as it built up over time
An acute injury, as it affected her performance
An acute injury, as it came from running
A chronic problem, as it came from a single fall
b.why: Her symptoms built up over months from too much training and too little rest, which fits overtraining syndrome, a chronic problem. Poor performance alone does not make something acute. Acute injuries come from a sudden event.
b.clue: Think about how long the problem took to develop.

a.best: A sprained ankle from landing badly after a jump

b.best: A chronic problem, as it built up over time
